key_insight: PosteriorBench argues that evaluating generative inverse solvers by a single best reconstruction is not enough. The paper shifts the focus from point estimates to posterior matching, so methods are judged on whether they capture the full set of plausible solutions and their uncertainty.
problem_solved: Current benchmarks for inverse problems often reward methods that produce one plausible output, even when the true problem is ambiguous. This can hide failures such as mode collapse, overconfident predictions, and poor uncertainty calibration in ill-posed scientific inverse settings.
method: Proposes a benchmark framework centered on posterior matching rather than only reconstruction accuracy.
Evaluates whether generated solutions reflect the full posterior distribution over possible answers for a given observation.
Exposes errors that point-metric evaluations miss, including missing modes and miscalibrated uncertainty.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this provides a more realistic way to compare generative inverse solvers in scientific applications. It encourages building models that are not only accurate, but also probabilistically faithful and reliable under ambiguity.
visual_elements: Side-by-side comparison of point-estimate evaluation vs posterior-matching evaluation
Diagram showing one observation mapping to multiple valid inverse solutions
Distribution plots highlighting mode collapse and uncertainty miscalibration
Benchmark scorecard with metrics for reconstruction quality and posterior fidelity
paper_title: PosteriorBench: From Point Estimates to Posterior Matching in Evaluating Generative Inverse Solvers
paper_authors: Jiachen Yao, Zi-Siang Hsu, Xi Deng, Aditi Gupta, Xin Ju
